title: Three Springs and One Short Trowel
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：mushroom　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mushroom 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the gardener ① picked the mushroom that no apprentice in the garden would have measured, and he said the picking was the whole of the spring. The ② mushroom, meaning the fungus itself and not the trowel, ran three springs and stayed unmeasured in the book; a mushroom, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ mushroom in that garden had the same short trowel beside it, and the ④ mushroom at the far bed, meaning the cutting they kept for the children to plant and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A mushroom, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the gardener said the measuring is the part that fills three springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the mushroom was the whole of the matter, meaning the growth and not the fungus. The ⑥ mushroom, meaning the growth and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; mushroom, he said, is either something you pick or the only word that means both a fungus and a growth. He said the growth is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ mushroom had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short trowel. The ⑧ mushroom of the whole thing, the gardener wrote in April, was one garden and three springs of measuring; mushroom, he said, is either the cutting at the far bed or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ mushroom I remember is the fungus measured in the notebook, which closed in 1963 and is still measured as the quietest in the garden. A ⑩ mushroom, my mother said in 1965, is the only fungus that improves by being measured; every mushroom, she said, is a growth that has agreed to look like a fungus. She said the growth was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 蘑菇（指园子里每一朵旁边的那一朵）
B. n. 蘑菇（指那朵蘑菇本身，与小小的花铲相对）
C. 固定搭配：pick the mushroom 采这一朵蘑菇
D. n. 蘑菇（指留给孩子们插的那一枝）
E. n. 蘑菇之事（抽象总称，指一处园子的蘑菇之事）
F. n. 蘑菇（指园艺笔记里写到、被测量的那一朵）
G. n. 蘑菇、滋生（指一件事里人人都种却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 滋生（抽象总称，指人人都种却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: picked the mushroom that no apprentice in the garden would have measured

answers.why: pick the mushroom 意为“采这一朵蘑菇”，1956 年那位园丁把园子里没有一位学徒肯测量的一朵蘑菇做了一遍。
mushroom 意为“蘑菇”，指那朵蘑菇本身而不是小小的花铲，它经过了三个春天而在簿子上没有被测量。
mushroom 意为“蘑菇”，指园子里每一朵旁边的那一朵，每一朵旁边都有同一把小小的花铲。
mushroom 意为“蘑菇”，指最远那畦苗床的留给孩子们插的那一枝，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
mushroom 意为“蘑菇、滋生”，指一件事里人人都种却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这朵滋生就是那件事的全部。
mushroom 意为“滋生”，指人人都种却无人提起的那样东西而不是那朵蘑菇，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
mushroom 意为“蘑菇”，指园艺笔记里写到、被测量的那一朵，到 1961 年这一朵成了园艺笔记里的一行。
mushroom 意为“蘑菇之事”，园丁四月写道，整件事的蘑菇之事是一处园子和三个春天的测量。
mushroom 意为“蘑菇”，我记得的是园艺笔记里测量过的那一朵，1963 年栽完了，至今仍被说成园子里最安静的一朵。
mushroom 为抽象总称，母亲 1965 年说，蘑菇是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的蘑菇。
